Follow-up from PR #358 Copilot review (106.033-T), two related findings:

(1) ShipShipment's locked closure (internal/core/shipment_lifecycle.go) has no compensating rollback for completeReleaseScope/returnUnreleasedFeatureItems/setArtifactStatus mutations when a LATE failure occurs immediately before the final moveShipmentStatusWithHeadGuard persist (e.g. the new 106.033-T head-drift refusal, but also any pre-existing late failure such as a persistArtifact I/O error or hook failure). A refusal at that point leaves release-scope items/features already mutated (done) while the shipment itself stays active -- a partially-applied release.

(2) moveShipmentStatusWithHeadGuard's repository-ref CAS re-check (internal/core/shipment.go) is the last read the guard FUNCTION performs, but persistArtifact itself still does further non-mutating preparation afterward (artifact validation, FindArtifactPath resolution, registry load, two file snapshots, potential target-directory creation) before its own first mutating filesystem write -- widening the residual window this guard narrows but does not eliminate. A repository-wide tightening would mean moving the guard inside persistArtifact itself, immediately before its first mutating write -- but persistArtifact is the shared persistence path for EVERY artifact type (tasks, features, shipments), not just shipment-status transitions, so threading a shipment-specific expected-head parameter through it is a materially larger design surface than 106.033-T's declared scope.

Both are comparable in shape to the git-ref-lock option (b) the 126-S stage memory already explicitly deferred for having a materially larger design surface, and were intentionally out of scope for 106.033-T. Investigate/implement as a dedicated follow-up: (a) a rollback or reconciliation mechanism (e.g. doctor-detectable partial-release state, or an explicit compensating undo of completeReleaseScope/setArtifactStatus on any late ShipShipment failure), and (b) a repository-wide (not shipment-specific) persistArtifact-level CAS/guard design, evaluated together since both touch the same "last read before persist" boundary.
